title: Three Days and One Short Coin
subtitle: 日常生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）
meta: 主题语境：日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）　|　核心词汇：luck　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 luck 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1985 the neighbour ① tried the luck that no stranger in the street would have recorded, and he said the trying was the whole of the day. The ② luck, meaning the chance itself and not the coin, ran three days and stayed unrecorded in the book; luck, he said, is the only thing in a street that is judged by how long it is left unrecorded.

Every ③ bit of luck in that street had the same short coin beside it, and the ④ luck at the far doorstep, meaning the token they kept for the children to keep and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. Luck, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to record; the neighbour said the recording is the part that fills three days.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the luck was the whole of the matter, meaning the fortune and not the chance. The ⑥ luck, meaning the fortune and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody records; luck, he said, is either something you try or the only word that means both chance and a fortune. He said the fortune is the part they remember.

By 1990 the ⑦ luck had become a line in a note, and the note had become an argument about the short coin. The ⑧ luck of the whole thing, the neighbour wrote in May, was one street and three days of recording; luck, he said, is either the token at the far doorstep or the reason you learned to record. He said the recording was never mentioned.

The ⑨ luck I remember is the luck recorded in the note, which closed in 1992 and is still recorded as the quietest in the street. ⑩ Luck, my mother said in 1994, is the only thing that improves by being recorded; all luck, she said, is a fortune that has agreed to look like chance. She said the fortune was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 运气；机遇（指街口里每一点旁边的那一点）
B. n. 运气；机遇（指那点运气本身，与硬币相对）
C. 固定搭配：try the luck 碰这一点运气
D. n. 运气；机遇（指留给孩子们留着的那一枚那一点）
E. n. 运气之事（抽象总称，指一处街口的运气之事）
F. n. 运气；机遇（指便条里写到、被记下的的那一点）
G. n. 运气、福气（指一件事里人人都盼却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 福气（抽象总称，指人人都盼却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: tried the luck that no stranger in the street would have recorded
The luck, meaning the chance itself and not the coin
Every bit of luck in that street
the luck at the far doorstep
the luck was the whole of the matter
the luck had become a line in a note
The luck of the whole thing

answers.why: try the luck 意为“碰这一点运气”，1985 年那位邻居把街口里没有一位路人肯记下的一点运气做了一遍。
luck 意为“运气；机遇”，指那点运气本身而不是硬币，它经过了三个日子而在簿子上没有被记下。
luck 意为“运气；机遇”，指街口里每一点旁边的那一点，每一点旁边都有同一枚小小的硬币。
luck 意为“运气；机遇”，指最远那道门槛留给孩子们留着的那一枚那一点，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
luck 意为“运气、福气”，指一件事里人人都盼却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这份运气就是那件事的全部。
luck 意为“福气”，指人人都盼却无人提起的那样东西而不是那点运气，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
luck 意为“运气；机遇”，指便条里写到、被记下的的那一点，到 1990 年这一点成了便条里的一行。
luck 意为“运气之事”，邻居五月写道，整件事的运气之事是一处街口和三个日子的记下。
luck 意为“运气；机遇”，我记得的是便条里记下过的那一点，1992 年用尽了，至今仍被说成街口里最安静的一点。
luck 为抽象总称，母亲 1994 年说，运气是唯一会因为被好好记下而变得更好的运气。
